newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-S.AFRICA PLANS REGIONAL SUPER 12 SIDES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-S.AFRICA PLANS REGIONAL SUPER 12 SIDES.

text.p: South Africa is to copy New Zealand by fielding regional sides in the southern hemisphere's Super 12 competition from next season, the South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) said on Friday.
South Africa would still have four sides in the competition but these would be drawn from 14 provincial rugby unions, SARFU chief executive officer Rian Oberholzer said in a statement.

"The New Zealanders have shown how successful the regional system can be and I am happy that the executive committee has decided to go ahead with the system proposed," Oberholzer said after a meeting of the SARFU executive committee on Friday.
"In this new system, all players in South Africa will be given the chance to compete for places in the Super 12 and, in turn, the Springbok team.
"Players from smaller provinces will be able to test themselves on a higher level and we are confident that those who are given the chance will perform up to expectations."

The four South African regions for the 1998 Super 12 would be drawn from: region one (Northern Transvaal, North West, Mpumalanga and Gauteng Falcons), region two (Western Province, South Western Districts and Boland), region three (Natal, Border and Eastern Province) and region four (Gauteng Lions, Free State, Northern Free State and Griqualand West).

"In the end it's good for South African rugby as talented players from provinces such as South Western Districts, Boland and Griqualand West -- who have all had exceptional results in the season so far -- can be utilised in the Super 12," Oberholzer said.
"The smaller provinces will also be given the chance to host a major Super 12 fixture and that's good news for the development of rugby in the rural areas."
Oberholzer also said that SARFU vice-president Mluleki George would chair an International Rugby Board committee on rugby development in the sub-Sahara region of Africa.
He said the first step for this committee would be to organise a sub-Sahara championship, to be hosted in South Africa early next year, featuring teams from over 20 countries.
